Pending projects for rail safety
*61. SHRI NILOTPAL BASU: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that several projects
related to Rail safety in terms of track renewal
rolling stock replacement/repair of Railway
bridges are pending; and
(b) if so, the details thereof, date wise
and Zone-wise?
Central teams for drought affected
States
*62. DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the State Governments have
yet to give clearance for Central teams to
visit their States and assess the drought
damage, before funds could be released
under the Natural Calamity Contingency
Fund;
(b) if so, whether the affected States had
submitted memoranda to the Centre, asking
for funds from NCCF, to tackle the drought
situation;
(c) if so, which States the Central teams
have visited and were planning to visit;
(d) what is the total damage caused by
drought; and
(e) what steps were taken by the affected
States to meet the situation?
Export of medicinal plants
*63. SHRIMATI N. P. DURGA :
DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) what bottlenecks India is facing in
playing a major role in the supply of
medicinal and herbal plants for the global
herbal medicine and cosmetics industry; and
(b) the agencies involved in
encouraging farmers to use latest
technological developments for better and
quicker yields of such plants and
selling the produce in the global
market?

International decade for culture of
peace and non-violence
*64. SHRI AIMADUDDIN AHMED
KHAN (DURRU): Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether in view of the United
Nations' declaring 2001-2010 as the
International decade for a culture of peace
and non-violence for the children of the
World, Government have drawn out
elaborate programmes for the children of
India; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps
taken or proposed to be taken in this regard?
Deletion of objectionable portions from
text books
*65. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Centre and the National
Council for Education Research and
Training (NCERT) have conveyed to the
Supreme Court that they were willing to
delete from textbooks the portions termed
as objectionable;
(b) if so, whether Government had
changed the school syllabi to promote a
particular political and religious
ideology;
(c) whether the objectionable portions
have been removed from the syllabi;
and

refused to implement the National
Curriculum Framework for school education
imposed through the NCERT syllabus and
textbooks in their States?
Foodgrains and financial assistance for
drought affected States
*66. SHRI K. NATWAR SINGH: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that relief is not
reaching the drought affected victims;
(b) if so, what is the total assistance
provided to drought affected States, in terms
of foodgrains and financial assistance;
(c) how much was made available to the
drought victims;
(d) what was their total demand; and
(e) to what extent it fell short of?
Closure of Sindri and Durgapur
fertilizer units
*67. SHRI DIPANKAR MUKHER-
JEE: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the news-item, captioned,
‘‘Government may revive FCI, HFC units
in Bihar, West Bengal,” appearing in
‘Business Standard’ dated 29th September,
2002;
(b) whether Government are re-
considering their decision to close down
units of Sindri and Durgapur, as reported in
the aforesaid news-item;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) if not, the reasons therefor;
(e) whether Government are also
considering delaying the closure of these
units, by at least a year, as reported in the
news -item; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?

Disparities in UGC grants
*68. SHRI P.  C. ALEXANDER: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 86 per cent of
non-plan grants released by the UGC during
2000-2001, have gone to Central
Universities and the Deemed Universities
leaving the State Universities with only a
marginal share of these funds;
(b) whether gross disparities also exist
in the grant of non-plan assistance between
colleges affiliated to Central Universities and
those to the State Universities; and
(c) if the answer to parts (a) and (b)
above be in the affirmative, whether the
UGC would be asked to ensure that the
State Universities and the colleges affiliated
to them get a more equitable share of these
funds?
Athletic tracks in Himachal Pradesh
*69. SHRI ANIL SHARMA: Will the
Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND
SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any proposal from Himachal Pradesh
Government for construction of athletic
tracks in Bilaspur, Kangra and Mandi;
(b) if so, what are the details thereof;
and
(c) what action Government have taken/
propose to take in the matter?
Additional relief to rain-deficient
States
*70. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether nine rain-deficient States
have sought Rs. 16,741.96 crore additional
relief from the Centre;
(b) if so, whether these States have
sought relief from Natural Calamity
Contingency Fund;
(c) whether this demand is in addition to
the second instalment of Rs. 809 crore
already released; and
(d) if so, to what extent the demand of
these States for additional relief from NCCF
has been accepted by Government?
Construction of public toilets along
Yamuna river
*71. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Japan Bank for
International Cooperation (JBIC) has called
upon his Ministry to investigate into the
haphazard and ill-planned construction of
public toilet blocks across the capital under
the Yamuna Action Plan, Phase-I;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government’s reaction thereto; and
(c) the action taken by Government in
this regard?
Foodgrain production
*72. SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether widespread drought in
twelve States in the country has killed India’s
hopes of a repeated good food production
this year;
(b) if so, whether experts see little change
of India having a foodgrains production of
208 million tonnes, like in 1999-2000, or

22
WIN2\SESSION\3749RS-QUES 22
the record production of 212 million tonnes
in 2001-2002;
(c) if so, to what extent it has affected
the foodgrains production; and
(d) what is the foodgrains target set
during the year 2002-2003?
Assistance to drought affected Andhra
Pradesh
*73. SHRI N. R. DASARI:
SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) which districts in Andhra Pradesh
have been affected by the recent drought;
(b) what is the extent of loss incurred
and the estimated shortfall in Kharif
production in the State;
(c) what is the financial assistance
sought by the State Government for relief
measures and the amount sanctioned by the
Union Government; and
(d) whether any steps have been taken
to supply seeds, free of cost, to the poor
farmers affected by the drought; if so, the
details thereof?
Meetings of Central Advisory Board
on Education
*74. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of times Central Advisory
Board on Education met during the last three
years, year-wise; and
(b) the decisions taken in these meetings
and the steps taken to implement them?
Modernisation of FPIs in Assam
*75. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have allotted
any funds to Assam Government for
expansion, modernisation and setting up of
food processing industries in the State
including the industries based on fruits and
vegetables during the last three years;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) whether Government have launched
any scheme in this regard; if so, the details
thereof?
Problem of cattle food
*76. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE  be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the problems faced by agriculturists owning
cattle farms due to the shortage of cattle
food like grass etc. whenever the country is
affected by natural calamities like floods and
drought; and
(b) if so, the details of remedies proposed
by Government to save the poor
agriculturists from this crisis?
Accident of Rajdhani Express
*77. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE:
SHRI RAMA  MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
 Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a rail accident took place on
the fateful night of 9th September, 2002

23
WIN2\SESSION\3749RS-QUES 23
when the Delhi bound Rajdhani Express
plunged into a river near Gaya;
(b) if so, the details thereof, including
the number of people who died/were injured
in this accident, the compensation paid to
dependents of the deceased and injured;
(c) whether any inquiry was ordered to
investigate the reasons of the accident; if so,
the details thereof; and
(d) whether the enquiry report has since
been received; if so, the findings thereof;
(e) the action proposed to be taken in
this regard and to eliminate recurrence of
such accidents?
Fall in Kharif production
*78. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY:
SHRI BALKAVI BAIRAGI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether his attention has been drawn
to the news-item which appeared in the
‘Economic Times’, dated 25th September,
2002, titled ‘‘Kharif grain production may
fall 18 per cent to 90.8 m. tonne’’;
(b) what is the current estimate of
foodgrains and oilseeds production in this
Kharif season and the measures initiated by
Government to tide over the crisis in case of
shortfall; and
(c) the relief provided to the affected
farmers?
Hike in tuition fees in Kendriya
Vidyalayas
*79. DR. ABRAR AHMED : Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Expenditure Reforms
Commission (ERC), set up by the Union
Government, has recommended a hike in
the tuition fees in Kendriya Vidyalayas; if
so, the details thereof; and
(b) whether Government have since
accepted this recommendation?
Scrapping of Railway projects
†*80. SHRI HARENDRA SINGH
MALIK: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Prime
Minister’s Office has asked the Ministry of
Railways to consider scrapping all those
projects which were approved 10 years back
or prior thereto but work has not started on
them;
(b) if so, the State-wise and project-wise
details thereof and the reasons for not
starting the projects; and
(c) what is the reaction of the Ministry
thereto?

Oilseeds production and price
331. SHRI C.O. POULOSE: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of production and price
per quintal of various oilseeds in the country
during the period 1991—2001, year-wise;
(b) the details of edible oil imported into
the country during the above period, year-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that the prices of
oilseeds registered a continuous fall during
this period;

resulted in the fall of prices; and

Accidents in agriculture sector
332. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:

for insurance or payment of compensation
to the victims of accidents in the agriculture
sector is in operation in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the number of farmer victims of
accidents who were compensated
during the last three years, year-wise and
district-wise?
Deporting breeding cattle
imported by A.P.
333. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government had asked the
Andhra Pradesh Government to deport 200
breeding cattle, imported from Australia in
the recent past;

Government in this regard?

state:

Crop Insurance Scheme in Himachal
Pradesh, District-wise;

meetings between farmers and Government

said scheme in the State, if so, what are the

National Agricultural Insurance Scheme?
Unit for measuring crop loss under
NAIS

the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:

make provision to take panchayat as a unit

block as a unit, as it is there now for the
purpose of National Agricultural Insurance
Scheme (NAIS); and

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be

KVKs in U.P.

'SURYA': Will the Minister of

opening KVKs in Uttar Pradesh;

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be

(a) what is the amount sought by
Karnataka to tackle the drought;

2002-2003; and
(c) the amount recommended by the
Central team for Karnataka to tackle the

20 per cent as budgetary support and 25

Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation;

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be

(a) whether a nine-member Central team
visited Hyderabad, to assess the damage

drought in Andhra Pradesh;

(b) the number of cultivators falling prey
to drought;

(d) the details of extent of efforts made

crops?

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have drawn up
any contingency plan to tackle the
devastating drought, witnessed in various

(b) if so, the details thereof;

KHAN (DURRU): Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Punjab and other State
Governments had demanded early
announcement of Minimum Support Price

concessions for farmers in drought hit
States;

State Governments; and

the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Minimum Support Price
policy is in force in the country;
(b) if so, the details of Minimum Support
Prices for all agricultural products and
foodgrains earmarked during the last three
years;
(c) the measures taken by Government
to protect the interests of the farmers in case
the prices fall below Minimum Support

the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased

goods have been declining while the cost of

order to complete the pending agricultural

the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
various short term and long term measures

in some States due to drought on account of
scanty rainfall;

(c) to what extent the water crisis is likely

and

and
(d) what measures Government are
taking to increase the yield per acre in India?

paddy

AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) what is the reason of delay in the
announcement of Minimum Support Price

(b) whether it is  a fact that Government
agencies are not buying the paddy arriving
in the market inspite of their willingness;
and
(c) whether Government would prefer
to buy paddy through middlemen; if not, by
when Government would declare the
Minimum Support Price in order to get rid
the farmers of this problem and save them
